nodes.characterization_summary: Eu₂O₃/NiS₂ shows a uniform nanosheet structure array on the carbon cloth.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to characterize the morphology of the synthesized nanosheets. Eu₂O₃/NiS₂ showed a uniform nanosheet structure array on the carbon cloth.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms the existence of the heterojunction interface by element distribution state and crystal plane spacing calibration of rare earth oxide and transition metal sulfide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The existence of the heterojunction interface can be determined by the element distribution state in transmission electron microscopy (TEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), and the crystal plane spacing calibration of rare earth oxide and transition metal sulfide (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM clearly detects existence of two interfaces in Eu₂O₃/NiS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5, the existence of two interfaces was clearly detected by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image reveals existence of two interfaces in Eu₂O₃/NiS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S5, the existence of two interfaces was clearly detected by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of rare earth oxides and transition metal sulfides proving the existence of the heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks of rare earth oxides and transition metal sulfides in X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) also prove the existence of the heterostructure of rare earth oxides and transition metal sulfides (Figure S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows characteristic peak and depth analysis of rare earths; Ni and S content increase and O content decreases with depth, confirming the interface formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peak and depth analysis of rare earths in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and the content of Ni and S increase and the content of O decreases with the increase of the depth in XPS, which also confirms the formation of the interface between rare earth oxide and nickel disulfide (Figures S9-S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows negative chemical shift after Eu₂O₃ introduction, indicating decreased Ni valence state conducive to preoxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XANES fitting was performed on the nickel K-edge, (Figure 1d). According to the edge position, it infers that after the introduction of the rare earth Eu₂O₃ interface... the edge position of Ni K-edges shows a negative chemical shift.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Eu-O and Ni-S vibrations confirming heterojunction interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The difference of lifetime in the fluorescence lifetime spectrum and the assignment of an emission peak in the fluorescence spectrum, combined with the existence of Eu-O and Ni-S in Raman vibration, also become favorable evidence for the existence of the heterojunction interface (Figures S7 and S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: ATR-FTIR shows Eu₂O₃/NiS₂ has higher OH adsorption coverage at 3500 cm⁻¹ than NiS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ATR-FTIR spectra and isotope-labeled ATR-FTIR spectra show that Eu₂O₃/SiS₂ has a higher OH adsorption coverage at the 3500 cm⁻¹ beam than NiS₂ (Figure 3a,b).
